I

Lesson 1 of 7 · Your character

Choose who
takes the first step.

Your name and appearance introduce you. Your attribute points decide where your strengths begin.

Begin with Appearance, Attributes and Personality. In a New Game, spend all 12 attribute points, with no more than five in any one trait. Review your choices before entering the world: your attribute points are fixed for that journey. After completing your journey you can begin again in New Game+ and New Game++, with 18 and 25 points and tougher foes.

Strength adds Attack Power. Agility adds Stealth. Stamina and Vitality enlarge their resources. Charisma gives you a head start with factions and people.

A level gained does not automatically add attribute points.

Your voice can grow.

Distribute 15 starting personality points, in steps of five, between Witty, Empathetic and Bold. Styled dialogue replies can develop those scores later. Your manner of speaking is separate from Karma and moral choices.

Grow through the skill tree.

Spend skill points from Player Info, Skills. Seven branches cover melee, magic, stealth, speech, utility, techniques and dirty tricks. Purchases are permanent.

II

Lesson 2 of 7 · Combat & stamina

Face the danger.
Keep a way out.

Stamina pays for commitment. Spend it with an eye on the attack that follows.

Block, parry, or move.

A block reduces damage from the front. Attacks from the side or rear receive no guard bonus. Blocking still spends Stamina; a block you cannot afford breaks your guard.

A shield parry begins with a well-timed block press. Watch the melee attacker’s glow: the half-second window can prevent the hit and stagger them. You still pay the normal blocked-hit Stamina cost.

A dodge needs movement. While moving, press Q or click the controller’s right stick to roll in that direction. Standing still will not dodge, and a dodge cannot interrupt your own attack, technique or cast.

15Dodge Stamina
50Technique Stamina
100Physical Ultimate Stamina

These are base costs. The Evasive perk reduces a dodge to 11.25 Stamina.

Magic, weapon techniques and physical Ultimates cannot be parried. Techniques and physical Ultimates can still be blocked.

Techniques and Ultimates.

Every weapon has a technique, and a powerful Ultimate you unlock in the skill tree. Some people in the world will teach you an alternate Ultimate, but only if they like you enough.

Move quietly.

Crouch to move quietly and stay out of sight. A detection eye shows how visible you are. Walls break sight; footsteps do not. Sneak up behind a target for a stronger strike.

One more breath

Stamina regeneration resumes one second after you spend it. The Recovery perk halves that delay. Leave time between commitments when you can.

III

Lesson 3 of 7 · Relief magic

First, place the Relief.
Then enter its influence.

Magic has a place in the world. A Relief in your hands must be deployed before its influence can help you cast.

Wield the school’s Relief and deploy it in front of you. As the board settles and grows, its influence spreads. Stand within that influence while holding a matching Relief to begin casting.

A friend’s board can serve you.

It must be deployed, available and of the same school as the Relief you hold. Only one caster can use a board at a time. If no suitable board is free, a refused cast costs nothing.

Know the price.

Most Blood spells spend Stamina and a share of maximum Health. You need more Health than the sacrifice. Dark spells add 1 to 10 Dark Points each, depending on their power; reaching 100 permanently corrupts your character.

When the sky darkens.

Now and then the sun or moon is eclipsed. Magic grows stronger beneath it: spells hit harder, and Holy and Blood spells cost less Stamina. Creatures that wield Reliefs grow stronger too.

What does corruption change?

Maximum Health, maximum Stamina and Stamina regeneration fall by 10%. Dark cooldowns become 25% shorter; Invisibility and Fear last 25% longer, and Void Pulse pushes 25% farther.

Corrupted characters cannot cast Holy magic or deploy a Holy Relief. Lowering Dark Points afterward does not cure corruption.

IV

Lesson 4 of 7 · Travel & preparedness

Prepare to go farther.
Remember the way back.

Exploration belongs to your character. So do the places you have personally discovered.

Unexplored ground is black on your map. As you move, you reveal the area within 60 metres. That knowledge stays with your character, even when friends are exploring somewhere else.

Walk into a travel waypoint to discover it and earn 100 XP once. Speak to a regional Cursed Doll to open her travel map. You can return to discovered waypoints with available arrival points; training is not required to unlock them.

A friend’s explored map does not become your explored map. Each player makes their own discoveries.

Before the next road

Check food and water. They start at 100 and 50, and diminish with time in the world, including time skipped by waiting. Their fullness limits are separate. Eating and drinking restores them and heals; let either run empty and you will suffer for it. Skill perks raise your limits.

Read the lock. Carry its key to Unlock, or Pick Lock through three to five timing prompts. A miss makes noise; being seen tampering can count as a crime.

Read the prompt. “Steal” and an owner’s name mean the item belongs to someone. A person who sees you take it can witness a theft.

Visit a Doll. Cursed Dolls stand in every region. Beside travel, a Doll offers a Training Arena where regional foes come one at a time for half XP and no loot. Dying there costs you nothing.

Ride a horse. Look at a horse and press Interact to mount. Weapons are put away while riding, and you cannot dodge. Hold Left Shift to gallop.

Night changes who walks the roads and when towns lock down.

V

Lesson 5 of 7 · People & choices

People remember.
In different ways.

A friendship, a reputation and a personality are separate parts of your life in the realm.

Helping or harming a named character changes how they regard you. That relationship can shape your dialogue. It is personal, too: someone may like you and feel differently about the friend beside you.

Karma is your moral record.

It runs from −100 to +100. Kind and cruel deeds move it, and it is separate from friendships, factions, your voice and Dark Points. You can check it on the Social and Codex page.

A faction has its own view.

Witnessed conduct, conversations and story events can change your standing with a faction. Your individual friendships remain separate.

Being seen matters.

A witness must see the act and recognize you to attach a personal consequence to you. Distance, cover, facing and concealment can affect identification. Darkness alone does not reliably hide violence or Dark casting.

Crime has a cost.

Crimes seen by a witness are reported. Guards may arrest you: surrender and serve a sentence, or pay your way out where the law allows. Your belongings wait in a chest outside the cell.

VI

Lesson 6 of 7 · Playing together

Four places by the fire.
Four stories on the road.

A campaign welcomes up to four human players. Two can play locally on each computer.

Host a lobby.

Host a game and the creator becomes a lobby: up to four players make their characters together. Each guest keeps a save in the host’s campaign and returns at the nearest Doll.

Find your companions.

Choose Join Game, then Refresh to browse the local network. Join with a new adventurer while the host is still creating the campaign. After the campaign begins, only the characters made in that lobby can rejoin. Join by Address offers the same choices for a typed host address.

For local play, a second player presses Start on a second controller during gameplay. The screen splits left and right. Keyboard, mouse and the first gamepad stay with Player 1; Player 2 uses their own gamepad and leaves by holding View/Back.

A local pair needs two free player spaces to join together. Wild creatures can be tamed and companions can join you; they never take a player’s seat.

Keep the party together.

Saving from the pause menu, a checkpoint or a quest saves connected characters and the shared world. The host manages the session’s save.

Yours to carry

Your conversations, choices and one-time rewards belong to your character. A friend finishing a scene does not automatically finish it for you.

A world you share

An opened door or a defeated boss affects the shared campaign. Your character’s progress and the state of the world are different things.

When a teammate falls

With another eligible human teammate alive, a fallen player has 60 seconds to be revived. A living player holds the interaction at their body for five seconds, restoring them in place with 15% Health.

After revival, that player cannot be downed again for one real-time hour. Waiting, reloading and travel do not shorten it. Solo play, Arena combat and some story defeats use immediate death instead.
